morning_memo: North Korea fired approximately 10 short-range ballistic missiles from Wonsan toward the East Sea, days after Seoul proposed military dialogue.
South Korea's National Intelligence Service told lawmakers Kim Jong Un may have used his Dandong visit to convey Pyongyang's position on US talks.
Prosecutors sought the death penalty for former President Yoon Suk Yeol over the December 3 martial law declaration.

bp_locations.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
bp_locations.note: As of April 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

bp_locations.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
bp_locations.note: As of May 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after 2+ years of fitting-out but was still not operational. New submarine construction begun in separate bay. NK Pro satellite analysis (Oct 20 2026) separately reports North Korea's Nampho Shipyard missed a deadline earlier in Oct 2026 to launch a 5,000-ton naval destroyer, with hull sections visible at two potential outdoor assembly areas.

bp_locations.name: THAAD Site, Seongju County
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: All 6 THAAD launchers were redeployed to the Middle East amid Iran tensions. At least 2 launchers may have returned to Seongju by late March 2026. Battery operational status remains uncertain. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: 2,500 kN engine test stand firing observed. Two villages razed for facility expansion. New seaport and large assembly building nearing completion. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: Road bridge construction accelerated, completion target moved to Summer 2026. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025. Ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
bp_locations.note: 38 North satellite imagery from October 16 confirms trucks traversing the New Yalu River (DPRK-Friendship) Bridge one day after the October 15 official opening, marking the start of commercial vehicle traffic. Daily NK reports customs delays leaving truck drivers waiting more than three hours. North Korea-China trade reached $299M in September 2026, the second-highest monthly total in 2026. Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 during his unannounced visit to Dandong, the first use of the bridge by the North Korean leader, nine days after its official opening.

bp_locations.name: Rason SEZ
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea NLL
bp_locations.note: As of September 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed the Northern Limit Line near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south. ROK Navy fired approximately 60 warning shots; vessel retreated after 1 hour. ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk stated October 20 2026 that North Korea has made 'various changes' to forces facing South Korea's border islands, with Seoul stepping up surveillance along the maritime border. 38 North satellite imagery published October 29 shows North Korea continuing to install new fencing along its border.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
bp_locations.note: As of January 27-28, 2026: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of the Provisional Measures Zone to Weihai shipyard following President Lee Jae-myung's Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Vostochny/Dunai
bp_locations.note: As of January 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice, one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked January 14 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since September 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels (Angara, Maria, Maya-1, Lady R) delivered approximately 15,800 containers (approximately 4.2-5.8 million munitions) from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

top_stories.headline: North Korea fires ~10 short-range ballistic missiles from Wonsan, days after Seoul dialogue offer
top_stories.body: North Korea launched a salvo of approximately 10 short-range ballistic missiles (SRBMs) from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea at around 12:30 p.m. Korea Standard Time on October 29, the ROK Joint Chiefs of Staff announced. The missiles flew approximately 250 km, with the US and South Korea conducting joint precision analysis. The launches came days after Defense Minister **Kang Shin-chul** publicly called on Pyongyang to return to dialogue at the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting Plus (ADMM-Plus) in the Philippines.

top_stories.headline: NIS: Kim Jong Un may have used Dandong visit to convey Pyongyang's position on US talks
top_stories.body: South Korea's National Intelligence Service told lawmakers in a closed-door intelligence committee audit that **Kim Jong Un** may have conveyed Pyongyang's stance on potential talks with the United States during his October 24 visit to Dandong, China. The NIS noted Kim was accompanied by senior diplomats including Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui rather than military officials, suggesting a purpose beyond commemorating China's Korean War anniversary participation. The NIS added that China could relay Kim's position to Washington but does not appear to have the will to act as a broker.

top_stories.headline: Prosecutors seek death penalty for former President Yoon Suk Yeol over December martial law
top_stories.body: South Korean prosecutors have requested the death penalty for former President **Yoon Suk Yeol** in connection with his December 3, 2025 declaration of martial law. The prosecution's demand represents the most severe penalty sought in the case against Yoon, who was impeached and removed from office following the failed declaration. The trial remains ongoing in Seoul.

also_today.body_text: South Korea's NIS told the National Assembly intelligence committee that a border-area resident made an erroneous report; Paju City officials said they could not determine what happened.

also_today.headline: Chinese travel agency claims invitation to organize youth tours to North Korea's Wonsan Kalma resort
also_today.body_text: A Chinese agency called Offline posted on social media it had been invited to run tours from late October, though a tourism insider expressed skepticism the trips will take place.

also_today.headline: 38 North quick take: Kim's Dandong trip was unusual and differs from past pre-summit China visits
also_today.body_text: 38 North analysis by Rachel Minyoung Lee notes Kim's October 24 same-day trip via the New Yalu River Bridge was framed around the Chinese People's Volunteer Army anniversary, diverging from the pattern of extended visits preceding diplomatic breakthroughs.

also_today.headline: President Lee vows to strengthen US-ROK alliance at Korean War battle ceremony
also_today.body_text: President **Lee Jae-myung** pledged to reinforce the alliance at a ceremony marking a Korean War battle, hours after North Korea's missile salvo.

also_today.headline: US Defense Secretary Hegseth meets ROK, Japan, India, Australia defense chiefs at ADMM-Plus in Philippines
also_today.body_text: US Defense Secretary **Pete Hegseth** held bilateral defense talks with his South Korean counterpart **Kang Shin-chul** on the sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting Plus, emphasizing the alliance is built on peace through strength.

rok_government.action: FM Cho Hyun departs for the US for G20 sherpa meeting and bilateral talks with Rubio
rok_government.detail: Foreign Minister **Cho Hyun** left for the United States to participate in a G20-related meeting and hold bilateral talks with US Secretary of State **Marco Rubio**. Separately, ROK G20 Sherpa Kim Hee-sang met with Indonesia's G20 Sherpa Edi Prio Pambudi on October 29 to discuss cooperation ahead of the December 14-15 Miami G20 summit and preparations for Korea's 2028 G20 presidency.

rok_government.action: NIS disciplines staff who followed unlawful December 3 martial law orders
rok_government.detail: The NIS announced that a special audit found approximately 10 staff members followed unlawful orders from former Director Jo Tae-yong and other political appointees on the day of the December 3 martial law declaration; those staff will face disciplinary action. The NIS reported this finding to the National Assembly intelligence committee audit.

calendar_watch.detail: The 2026 Korea Grand Festival, a national-scale consumption promotion integrating 40,000 businesses, runs October 29 through November 15.

calendar_watch.detail: ROK FM Cho Hyun travels to the US and ROK G20 Sherpa met with Indonesia's sherpa on Oct 29 to coordinate positions ahead of the December 14-15 Miami G20 summit.

rok_assembly.action: Closed-door NIS audit yields Kim China visit assessment and martial law discipline findings
rok_assembly.detail: Ruling Democratic Party Rep. Yoon Kun-young and People Power Party Rep. Yoo Yeong-ha both readout the NIS closed-door audit: Kim Jong Un may have conveyed US-talks intentions via his Dandong trip, North Korean loudspeaker reports were false, and about 10 NIS staff who obeyed martial law orders will be disciplined.

rok_assembly.action: Presidential secretariat audit disrupted over Kim Tae-gyu's participation
rok_assembly.detail: Ruling and opposition parties clashed at the reopened Blue House secretariat national audit over the participation of Kim Tae-gyu, with the Democratic Party demanding Kim apologize for denying that Yoon Suk Yeol and Chun Doo-hwan staged a coup; the session broke down before a non-participation agreement was reached.

business_economy.headline: SK Innovation posts record Q3 operating profit of 3.7 trillion won, up 533% year-on-year
business_economy.body_text: *3.7 trillion won* in Q3 operating profit was driven by improved petroleum product export margins and lubricant business strength; revenue rose 39.7% year-on-year to 28.8 trillion won.

business_economy.headline: Bank of Korea board member says won is moving faster than expected
business_economy.body_text: A Bank of Korea board member told Reuters the won is moving faster than anticipated, a signal of concern about exchange rate volatility at a time when the KOSPI fell 1.24% on October 29.

business_economy.headline: South Korea's communications regulator fines Google and Apple over app payment practices
business_economy.body_text: South Korea's media commission fined Google and Apple for unfair app market practices related to payment systems, extending Seoul's tech platform enforcement actions against US firms.

business_economy.headline: Bloomberg Fed's Warsh explains why he watches Korea's economy closely
business_economy.body_text: Federal Reserve Governor **Kevin Warsh** cited Korea's economy as a key leading indicator he monitors, pointing to its semiconductor export performance as a barometer for global technology demand.

business_economy.headline: Bithumb hack exposes personal data of 6,444 customers including passport numbers
business_economy.body_text: Cryptocurrency exchange Bithumb disclosed that a cyberattack on its internal systems leaked personal information of 6,444 customers, with 5,600 of those cases including identification document copies.

northeast_asia.headline: South Korean 'tilt' toward Russia alarms European allies, FT
northeast_asia.body_text: The Financial Times reports that South Korea's diplomatic positioning toward Russia has alarmed European partners, amid Seoul's parallel reduction in diplomatic personnel in Ukraine over the North Korean prisoner-of-war dispute.

northeast_asia.headline: Russia imports North Korean workers disguised as students, report shows
northeast_asia.body_text: A new investigation documents Russian firms and individuals disguising North Korean labor employment as education to circumvent international sanctions, linking those workers to companies supporting Russia's military-industrial complex.

northeast_asia.headline: China breaks nine-month silence on North Korea missile launches, calls for peace efforts
northeast_asia.body_text: China's foreign ministry broke a nine-month silence on North Korea's ballistic missile launches, expressing hope that all parties concerned will make efforts toward peace, stopping short of condemning Pyongyang.

opeds_today.headline: Bridge to Beijing? Kim Jong-un Crosses the Yalu
opeds_today.central_argument: Kim Jong Un's same-day October 24 crossing of the New Yalu River Bridge to Dandong represented a diplomatic signal distinct from past China visits, with his delegation of senior diplomats rather than military officials pointing to a US-engagement agenda rather than a pure alliance reaffirmation.
opeds_today.summary: CSIS analysis of Kim Jong Un's October 24 Dandong visit examines why the trip differs from prior patterns, specifically the presence of Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui and other diplomats rather than military officials, and Kim's use of the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge. The piece explores whether Beijing could serve as a conduit for Pyongyang's position on potential US talks.

opeds_today.headline: OPCON: Washington wants flexibility, Seoul wants control
opeds_today.central_argument: South Korea's push for wartime operational control transfer would give Seoul authority over Korean forces but would not give it a say over how the United States employs its own forces beyond the Korean Peninsula.
opeds_today.summary: Lowy Institute analysis examines the structural gap in the wartime operational control (OPCON) transfer debate: Seoul seeks command authority as a sovereignty marker, while Washington needs to retain flexibility over how US forces are used in broader contingencies beyond Korea. The piece contextualizes the October 29 announcement deferring the Security Consultative Meeting on OPCON to early 2027.

opeds_today.headline: How War Memorialization Legitimizes the Russia-DPRK Alliance and Strengthens Kim Jong Un's Legitimacy
opeds_today.central_argument: North Korea and Russia use shared Korean War and World War II memorialization, anchored by the new Tumen River road bridge and CPV anniversary events, to legitimize their military alliance domestically and internationally while reinforcing Kim Jong Un's leadership narrative.
opeds_today.summary: 38 North analyst Nika Pasko examines how war commemoration events, including the first road bridge linking Russia and North Korea across the Tumen River opened in September 2026 and the CPV anniversary activities surrounding Kim's Dandong visit, serve as institutional legitimation tools for the Russia-DPRK alliance. The analysis traces how memorialization of shared 'blood alliances' strengthens Kim's domestic authority while providing rhetorical cover for ongoing military cooperation.

top_articles.headline: North Korea Continues Installing New Fencing
top_articles.summary: 38 North satellite imagery analysis shows North Korea continuing to install new fencing along its border, extending the fortification trend documented throughout 2026.

top_articles.headline: North Korean journalists told to trade reporting duties for ideology drills marking journalists' union 80th anniversary
top_articles.summary: In Ryanggang province, North Korean journalists at the provincial party newspaper are required to set year-end loyalty pledges and attend mandatory ideological sessions that consume more time than normal reporting duties.

senior_officials.name: Choe Son-hui
senior_officials.activity: Accompanied Kim Jong Un on his October 24 Dandong visit, a delegation composition the NIS cited as evidence the trip had a diplomatic rather than purely ceremonial purpose.

kcna_delta.bottom_line: North Korea launched approximately 10 short-range ballistic missiles from Wonsan on October 29, days after the ROK defense minister called for dialogue; state media covered the Pyongyang trade fair and harvest mobilization but had not reported on the launches as of this digest.

capitol_hill.headline: US House introduces bill to block AI technology theft, names North Korea as country of concern
capitol_hill.body_text: The House introduced legislation to prevent AI technology theft, explicitly listing North Korea among countries of concern; the bill would restrict AI-related technology transfers that could benefit designated adversaries.

capitol_hill.headline: Report: South Korea has spent $363 million lobbying US lawmakers
capitol_hill.body_text: A report cited by Breitbart News states South Korea has spent $363 million lobbying US lawmakers, a figure that has attracted congressional attention amid broader scrutiny of foreign government lobbying disclosures.

korea_world.headline: South Korea says it is considering deployment options to the Strait of Hormuz, including aircraft
korea_world.body_text: Seoul confirmed it is reviewing options for a military deployment to the Strait of Hormuz, including the possibility of aircraft, as part of broader discussions about contribution to maritime security in the region.

korea_world.headline: South Korea has not ruled out severing diplomatic ties with Ukraine if POW escalation continues
korea_world.body_text: Seoul has not excluded the possibility of cutting diplomatic relations with Ukraine if the dispute over North Korean prisoner-of-war soldiers held by Kyiv continues to escalate; South Korea previously withdrew 8 diplomatic personnel from Ukraine.
